title: Speier et al. 2017 — A comparison of stimulus types in online classification of the P300 speller using language models
description: This dataset contains P300 speller EEG recordings from 10 healthy adult subjects, collected as part of a study comparing stimulus types (famous faces vs. inverting stimuli) in online classification of the P300 speller using language models. Each subject completed two sessions with three runs each, using a 6x6 character matrix row-column speller paradigm with visual feedback. The data were converted to BIDS format using MOABB from the original Speier et al. (2017) study.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a g.tec amplifier at 256 Hz sampling rate with 32 channels arranged per the standard_1005 montage, referenced to the left ear with ground at AFz. The paradigm was a P300 row-column speller with two stimulus conditions (Famous Faces, Inverting), presented online with visual feedback and a 6x6 character matrix. Stimulus onset asynchrony was 125 ms with a 25 ms inter-stimulus interval.
